    Finite half-words and their subspaces #

    A (finite) half-word at (v, s) is a walk C from v in which every letter starts with the sign nsign s of the prefix before it: s for the first letter, and the opposite of the end sign of the previous letter afterwards. At the end u of C the next sign n admits at most one direct continuation b (σ b = n) and one inverse continuation d (ε d = n), and C⁺ = C^*(M_u ∩ ker b), C⁻ = C^*(im d). Then C⁻ ≤ C⁺, inverse continuations lie below C⁻, and C⁺ lies below direct continuations.
